vocabulary.meaning: a general rise in prices that reduces the purchasing power of money
examples: Inflation is an important idea when discussing why are prices going up?.
Learning about inflation can help us understand this issue more clearly.

vocabulary.meaning: the amount of money needed to pay for basic everyday expenses
examples: People often have different views about cost of living when discussing why are prices going up?.
Understanding cost of living can make a conversation about this topic more precise.

vocabulary.meaning: the amount of goods and services that a given amount of money can buy
examples: The topic of why are prices going up? raises useful questions about purchasing power.
We can discuss how purchasing power affects people, communities, or the environment.

vocabulary.meaning: the relationship between how much of something is available and how much people want it
examples: Supply and demand can play an important role in debates about why are prices going up?.
Different countries may deal with supply and demand in different ways.

vocabulary.meaning: the percentage charged for borrowing money or paid on savings
examples: A discussion about why are prices going up? can include the effects of interest rate.
Knowing the meaning of interest rate makes it easier to express an opinion on this issue.

vocabulary.meaning: an increase in the amount of money required to buy something
examples: Price rise is useful vocabulary for talking about why are prices going up?.
We can use the idea of price rise to compare different experiences and viewpoints.
